results.title: Dissolved oxygen rise after valve work
results.text: A step rise in dissolved oxygen at the point of use shortly after maintenance on a valve or fitting upstream suggests air ingress through a leaking diaphragm or seal. Check the work-order history for recent valve work on assets upstream of the point of use. Corrective action: re-inspect and re-seat or replace the diaphragm, leak-test, and flush.

results.title: AMC rising in a process bay
results.text: Compare AMC at the make-up air inlet with AMC in the bay. If the inlet is steady while the bay rises, the chemical filtration stage is the likely source.

results.title: UV-185nm lamp ageing
results.text: UV lamp output falls as running hours accumulate. When lamp hours exceed the rated life, oxidation of organics becomes incomplete and TOC drifts upward, often with a falling UV intensity reading. Corrective action: plan lamp replacement, verify intensity after replacement, and re-measure TOC after the loop has flushed.

report.narrative: An investigation was conducted for the dissolved oxygen excursion at sensor tag UPW_B_DO_POU. The measured value was 2.4003 ppb against an upper limit of 1.0 ppb, resulting in a reading verdict of FAIL (E1). The rate of change analysis showed a slope per hour of 1.1204 ppb, with mean values rising from 1.4052 ppb in the first half to 2.396 ppb in the second half of the 120-minute window (E2). Asset dependencies and upstream tracing identify VALVE_B_07 directly upstream of POU_ETCH_1 (E7, E8). Recent work orders within 24 hours indicate that valve VALVE_B_07 was replaced on Loop B 2 hours prior (E4). Knowledge base article UPW-06 notes that a step rise in dissolved oxygen shortly after maintenance on an upstream valve or fitting suggests air ingress through a leaking diaphragm or seal (E5). Other runtime metrics show UV_B at 70.0 percent of rated life, POLISH_B at 51.1 percent, and RO_B at 64.6 percent, ruling out resin or lamp exhaustion (E9, E10, E11). The calibration was verified as valid (E1). Therefore, the root cause is determined to be a valve diaphragm leak.
recommended_actions: Re-inspect and re-seat or replace the diaphragm on VALVE_B_07 for qualified engineer review.
Perform a thorough leak test on the newly replaced valve and fitting components for qualified engineer review.
Flush the affected loop and monitor sensor tag UPW_B_DO_POU until readings stabilize below the 1.0 ppb limit for qualified engineer review.
